title: AP® Biology
subject: Biology
alignment: AP® Biology exam (unit order follows the usual course sequence; outline written in our own words)

units.title: Water, elements and the molecules of life
objectives: Explain how hydrogen bonding gives water the properties living things depend on
Relate the structure of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids to their jobs in cells
Describe how monomers join and split through dehydration and hydrolysis

units.title: Cells: parts, membranes and transport
objectives: Compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells and the roles of major organelles
Explain why surface area to volume ratio limits cell size
Predict the direction of water and solute movement across membranes, including by osmosis

units.title: Enzymes and how cells capture and release energy
objectives: Explain how enzymes lower activation energy and how temperature, pH and inhibitors change their rate
Trace energy and matter through photosynthesis
Trace energy and matter through cellular respiration and fermentation

units.title: Cell signaling, feedback and the cell cycle
objectives: Describe the steps of a signal transduction pathway
Distinguish positive and negative feedback with examples
Explain how checkpoints regulate the cell cycle and what happens when they fail

units.title: Meiosis and inheritance
objectives: Explain how meiosis and fertilization create genetic variation
Predict offspring ratios with Punnett squares and probability rules
Use a chi-square test to compare observed and expected results

units.title: DNA, gene expression and biotechnology
objectives: Describe DNA replication, transcription and translation
Explain how gene expression is regulated in prokaryotes and eukaryotes
Predict the effects of mutations, and describe common biotechnology methods such as PCR and gel electrophoresis

units.title: Evolution and natural selection
objectives: Explain how natural selection acts on variation in populations
Use the Hardy-Weinberg equations to test whether a population is evolving
Read phylogenetic trees and cladograms to infer relationships

units.title: Ecology: populations, communities and ecosystems
objectives: Model population growth with exponential and logistic equations
Trace energy flow and matter cycling through ecosystems
Predict how disruptions affect community structure and biodiversity
